newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares drift but traders see growth soon.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares drift but traders see growth soon.

text.p: Leading Russian shares drifted to close little changed on Wednesday in spotty trade, but some dealers said long-awaited growth could be just around the bend.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 leading shares closed slightly off at 290.22 after 291.32 on Tuesday. Total market turnover was a limp $26.1 million.
National power utility UES edged up to $0.2109 from Tuesday's closing $0.2090, while regional power company Mosenergo slumped to $1.229 from $1.241.
Oil company Surgutneftegaz was almost unchanged at $0.685 after $0.683.
"I'm seeing some sporadic buying and focused buying, people will buy UES today, Mosenergo tomorrow, Surgutneftegaz the next and so on," said ING Barings senior trader Peter Kizenko.
Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chhikvadze saw the market sticking at current levels in the near future, in part on uncertainty surrounding U.S. interest rates.
Some analysts say Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan may decide to raise rates at a Fed meeting in May in light of recent consumer price index data.
But other traders said slight gains in scattered first-tier shares could be the first signs of growth -- a trend which some analysts predicted would strengthen in May.
"I think the market is getting more active. There aren't any crazy buyers yet but the transfer from cash to shares is happening," said Creditanstaldt-Grant trader Andrei Galperin.
"In principle there's a lot of spare money on the market."
